definition: Alternating perspective is a virtual reality viewing arrangement in which a person can switch at will between first-person and third-person views of a virtual body. In the reported embodiment research, this option was associated with a strong sense of owning the virtual body, with effects stronger than third-person view alone and comparable to strong first-person experiences.

reasons: The claim that effects under alternating perspective were “comparable to strong first-person experiences” is not explicitly supported by the packet. The packet says subjective body ownership and reaction to threat were “generally stronger for first person perspective and alternating condition than for third person perspective,” but does not state comparability between alternating and first-person effects.

The definition’s phrasing “associated with a strong sense of owning the virtual body” is partly supported (the packet discusses “sense of embodying a virtual body” and illusory ownership), but the packet does not directly support the exact “owning … comparable to …” effect comparison language used in the definition.

The packet supports alternating between first- and third-person perspective at will in VR, but it does not support the added claim that the effects were “comparable to strong first-person experiences.”

“Strong first-person experiences” is not a stated comparison in the source; the source only says ownership and threat reactions were generally stronger for first-person perspective and alternating condition than for third-person perspective.
